notes: Packed token shards ready to feed straight into OLMo-core pretraining runs: the raw fuel, in training order-agnostic form, with a tokenizer pinned hard enough that token counts are falsifiable. Names carry corpus plus token budget, because the budget is the axis that distinguishes siblings (pretrain/dolma2-150b, pretrain/fineweb-edu-10b) - see DATASET-STANDARD.md section 2. THE FORMAT DEFAULT IS THE POINT: uint32 little-endian, headerless, extension .u32le.bin, NEVER .npy. OLMo-core memmaps these files from byte 0 (olmo_core/data/utils.py:158) and derives token count from raw file size (:233), so a real 128-byte .npy header would corrupt the leading tokens AND the count, silently. OLMo-core also defaults to dtype uint16 while these corpora are uint32, which halves the count if dtype is inferred rather than read - hence dtype is declared here and read by dataset_paths(), never guessed. THE TOKENIZER IS A PUBLISHED DEPENDENCY, NOT A HAND-TYPED PIN: publish tokenizer/dolma2-bpe once (profile tokenizer/v1), set tokenizer_dependency above, and every corpus depends_on it. The validator DERIVES vocab_size and eos_token_id from that published tokenizer.json (tokenizer_v1.derive_vocab) and the decode smoke test asserts every sampled id against the derived vocab_size (0 <= id < vocab_size) - so the bound is computed from real bytes, never a guess, and an inflated placeholder can no longer make that gate decorative. This replaces the old inline vocab_size/eos_token_id pins, which were unverifiable typed values. license.basis is an honest 'unknown' at the family level rather than a convenient 'ODC-By-1.0': this family will hold Dolma2 (ODC-By-1.0), FineWeb-Edu (ODC-By-1.0), and selection-method rebuilds of sources whose terms nobody has read, and section 3 is explicit that an honest unknown beats a false value and stays queryable in the catalog. Each dataset overrides license with its actual, checked terms. Per section 5 there is no -of-NNNNN in shard names: the surviving shard count is unknowable at write time because it depends on filtering that has not run yet; completeness is proven by path-set equality against the manifest instead. decode_smoke_test bounds are the section 7 defaults - they catch all-zeros shards, all-EOS shards, and the zero-filled tail a crashed writer leaves behind, all of which pass every checksum and size gate ever written.
